summary.text: Igneous rock is one of the three main rock types, formed when magma or lava cools and becomes solid.
Rock that hardens underground cools slowly and grows coarse, visible grains, while rock that hardens at the surface cools fast and ends up fine-grained or glassy.
Most of Earth's oceanic crust is igneous rock, and igneous rock forms about 15% of today's land surface.

items.prompt: You find an igneous rock whose mineral grains are large enough to pick out by eye. Where did it most likely harden?

options.label: In lava spilling down a volcano's side
Deep underground, surrounded by other rock
In ash thrown high into the air
In lava that flowed into cold seawater

items.explain: Magma that solidifies within the crust cools slowly, so intrusive rocks are coarse-grained with grains visible to the naked eye.

items.prompt: Why does magma trapped inside the crust take so long to cool?

options.label: The rock around it is an excellent heat insulator
Groundwater keeps pouring fresh heat into it
Gas bubbles inside it keep producing new heat
Pressure at depth stops heat from moving at all

items.explain: The country rock surrounding an intrusion insulates it very well, so the magma cools slowly.

items.prompt: Molten rock forms deep below and then works its way upward. What makes it rise?

options.label: Earth's spin flings it toward the surface
Ocean tides pull it up from below
Its magnetism draws it toward the poles
It is less dense than the rock it left

items.explain: Magma rises because it is less dense than the rock from which it was extracted.

items.prompt: Basalt lava is fairly runny. Felsic rhyolite magma can be up to how many times as viscous as basalt?

options.label: About 2 times
About 10 times
Up to 100 times
Up to 10,000 times

items.explain: Rhyolite is usually erupted at low temperature and can be up to 10,000 times as viscous as basalt.

items.prompt: A volcano is fed by very sticky, felsic magma full of dissolved water vapour. How is it likely to erupt?

options.label: In gentle, long, runny lava rivers
Quietly, with no gas or ash at all
Violently, in gas-driven explosions
Only underwater, as black smokers

items.explain: Rhyolitic volcanoes commonly erupt explosively, and felsic magmas often erupt violently as dissolved gases such as water vapour are released.

items.prompt: Geologists find it harder to tell volcanic rocks apart from one another than intrusive ones. Why?

options.label: Volcanic rocks are always the same color
Volcanic rocks are mostly fine-grained or glassy
Volcanic rocks contain no minerals at all
Volcanic rocks break apart as soon as they form

items.explain: Because volcanic rocks are mostly fine-grained or glassy, their minerals are hard to see, which makes the types harder to distinguish.
